newsletter:
# Morning Brief — June 4, 2026

The macro tone is constructively choppy rather than cleanly risk-on. SPY is +5% on the month with 82% of sectors above their 50-day, which is broad participation, but the regime vote is only TRANSITIONAL at 6/10 confidence and the put/call is dragging the score. Cross-asset signals are mixed in a way that argues for selectivity: copper +10% on 21d and a steepening curve point to reflation, yet DXY +0.78% and 10Y at 4.46% (up 93bps over 21d) are a tightening headwind, and oil -9% undercuts the clean cyclical narrative. VIX at 16.5 in contango is benign but the 24h pop of 2% says hedges are getting bid into the print. Net read: risk appetite is intact at the index level but the internals (5d breadth bearish 34% > bullish 31%) say the rally is getting narrower under the surface.

Leadership is unambiguously Technology — XLK +21% on 21d and ACCELERATING_BULLISH, with QQQ a distant second at +10.6%. That matters structurally because the rest of the tape (XLV, XLB, XLI, XLY all roughly flat to +2%) is essentially treading water, so the index is being carried by one sector. Semiconductors at +16.9% and Software-Infrastructure +5.8% are the engines, and the rotation tape confirms inflows into Consumer Electronics and Software-Infra with nothing being actively distributed.

For un-run setups, the better risk/reward is in names that haven't extended: AVGO and ADI in semis offer exposure to the leading group without chasing the parabolic names that already ran. PATH in Software-Infra and ETSY in Internet Retail are coiling — ETSY is interesting because Internet Retail is HOLDING_BULLISH on flow despite -7.7% on 21d, which is the classic basing-with-accumulation pattern. The names to be careful chasing are anything already priced for perfection in semis — the +16.9% group return means late entries are paying up for trajectory that's decelerating from accelerating to holding.

Rotation read: accelerating into Consumer Electronics and Software-Infrastructure, while Semis and Internet names are downshifting from acceleration to holding — still bullish, but the second derivative is fading. No outright outflows or trend flips yet, which is why I'd size tighter than the regime score implies: the tape is one-legged on Tech and the 5d breadth is already net negative.

Into tomorrow, watch two things: (1) the 10Y — another leg higher from 4.46% with DXY firm will eventually bite multiples in the exact names leading this tape; (2) whether XLI/XLB can convert copper's strength into actual price follow-through, because a broadening into cyclicals is what turns this from a narrow Tech melt-up into a durable regime. If neither happens, fade strength in extended semis and stay patient on the coiled un-runs.
